events.description:
TaskKind now carries epic, bug, refactor, tech_debt, spike, feature, chore and docs. Conventional Commits v1.0.0, which law 7 adopts, also defines perf, test, style, ci and build, so five accepted commit types still have no task kind and work matching them is filed as chore or feature. They were deliberately left out of CO-12 rather than added speculatively: a kind nothing uses is a kind nobody validates, and each one needs a decision about whether it changes the verification gate (a perf change must prove a measured improvement, which is stricter than any current kind).

EXPANDED 2026-11-08, after the docs kind showed what adding one kind costs.

EMPIRICAL CASE (git log subjects, 400 per repo): build is used in benchwork 17, chalkline 11, outfeed 6,
miter 5, root 5, storypole 4, common 3; test in storypole 3, outfeed 2, benchwork 2; ci in miter 2,
chalkline 2, benchwork 2; perf in storypole 2, chalkline 1, root 1; style in miter 1. So these are not
speculative categories: they are commit types in daily use that the tracker cannot express, and work
matching them is filed as chore or feature today.

SCOPE, now including the structural fix. Adding docs required five hand-maintained enumerations: the
contract enum, the CLI KIND_NAMES array, the CLI parse_kind, the MCP parse_kind, and the MCP schema
enum. Doing that five more times by hand is five more chances to drift, and the schema copy fails
invisibly because a client reads it before calling. So: TaskKind::ALL and TaskKind::as_str (plus a
from_str that round-trips through serde) become the single source, the CLI and MCP lists derive from
them, and a test asserts the MCP schema's advertised enum equals ALL. Adding a kind then touches one
file and the compiler points at the rest.

PERF CARRIES A GATE OBLIGATION. Law 12 says no change may be called faster without a before/after
measurement recorded in three places. A perf kind that does not require one is worse than no perf kind:
it licenses the exact false-completion this work has been removing. The obligation is recorded on SP-40
(verify gates) rather than enforced here, because the gate belongs with the other refusals.

LIVE 2026-11-08, installed binary v0.1.0-beta.5, in a scratch git repo:

  --kind TECH-DEBT                 -> TechDebt (the tolerant parse also accepts techdebt)
  --kind wip                       -> unknown kind `wip`; expected one of: epic, feature, refactor, bug,
                                      tech_debt, spike, chore, docs, perf, test, style, ci, build

The list in that message is generated from TaskKind::ALL, which is the single source the CLI and MCP schema
now derive from. Commits: 641e70e (contract), 73355f0 (CLI and MCP), 3dab4a9 (test split), merged as
8769ccc.

Three files crossed the 250-line limit while this landed and were split rather than trimmed: task.rs into
task_kind.rs and task_scope.rs, storypole_wire.rs into task_kind_wire.rs, and schema.rs into
tests/schema_kinds.rs. The common chain refused to certify the task until the last of those was fixed.

PROCESS FAILURE worth recording: the three common commits were made while HEAD sat on
feat/gb-342-docs-kind, and the follow-up git push origin main pushed an unchanged main and reported
success - the commits reached origin only after an explicit merge (8769ccc). The receipt for this task
names feat/gb-342-docs-kind as its branch, which is accurate but is not where the work now lives. Pushing a
ref is not the same as publishing your work.
